texts.preamble: Jagjeet Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 February, 2016 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Bench At Indore S.B.:- Hon'ble Smt. Justice S.R. Waghmare Mcrc 222/2016 Jajitsingh s/o. Harvansh Singh Ji Tuteja vs. State of M.P. through Food Inspector, Dewas Mcrc 243/2016 Jajitsingh s/o. Harvansh Singh Ji Tuteja vs. State of M.P. through Food Inspector, Dewas
texts.facts: These are two applications filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. being filed by the same petitioner against the orders of the trial Court; whereas M.Cr.C. No.222/10 pertains to the dismissal of the application filed by the petitioner for transfer of the petition under Section 408 of the Cr.P.C. by the trial Court in Criminal Case No.4106/2010 and also upheld by the District Judge, Dewas on 21.12.2015 and both the orders have been impugned in the present petition. Whereas Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.243/16 has been filed by the petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 17.12.2015 passed by the 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Dewas upholding the order passed in the same original case No.4106/10. 02. Briefly stated the facts of the case are that the petitioner was being proceeded against for offence under Section 20-A of the Food Adulteration Act and Section 319 of the Cr.P.C. The respondent Food Inspector had taken samples of paneer (cottage cheese) from the Natraj Dairy belonging to the petitioner on 25.05.2010. During inspection the Inspector was however categorically informed by the petitioner that the paneer sample that was purchased by him from the Natraj Dairy on A.B. Road, opposite Rajesh Lodge and purchased from Ramesh Ahuja's shop. The bill was properly given by Paresh Ahuja who was the Manager and the same was given to the Food Inspector. The petitioner informed Inspector that the paneer was neither sold by the petitioner nor manufactured by him. However, the samples were taken by the Inspector along with samples of flour and the licence was handed over by the petitioner to the Food Inspector. The charge-sheet was issued by the Inspector under Sections 20-A of the Food Adulteration Act under Section 319 of the Cr.P.C. On 22.09.2015 the Counsel for the petitioner could not remain present. However, in the presence of the accused, Jagjeet Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104226808/ 1 the trial Court under Section 16-A of the Food Adulteration Act adopted the summary procedure and taking cognizance under Section 16-1(A) of the Food Adulteration Act, decided to conduct the trial under the warrants trial and thus converted the summary trial into a warrant trial. One prosecution witness i.e. PW1 Ms. Deepali Kange was discharged after examining her and the accused himself stated that since his Counsel is not available after framing of charge, this witness would be cross- examined. At this instance, the A.D.P.O. submitted that he did not want to examine any prosecution witness and, therefore, the trial Court, listed the matter for hearing on framing of charge. Being aggrieved the petitioner filed Criminal Revision No.83/2015, whereby the petitioner submitted that the matter had been pending for 5 years and the evidence of witnesses was not recorded and suddenly in the absence of the Counsel for the petitioner on 22.09.2015 converted the summary trial into warrants trial and such an order was contrary to the provisions of law and the petitioner ought to have been given opportunity of hearing before the conversion. The trial Court had also lost sight of the fact that the paneer was purchased by the petitioner himself for his use in the hotel and had neither it has been manufactured by him nor sold by him and, therefore, one opportunity of hearing ought to have been given to the petitioner; whereas in the absence of the Counsel, the trial Court straight away proceeded to convert the trial and list the matter for framing the charges. 03.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the petitioner has also vehemently opposed the fact that the petitioner never admitted that the matter may be converted to a warrants trial despite which the trial Court has in the order impugned observed so and then in these circumstances the order impugned was contrary to the provisions of law and principles of natural justice and hence present petitions be allowed as already stated above. 04. Counsel vehemently urged that once having come to the conclusion that a summary trial was required on 11.02.2011, the Presiding Officer had recorded the plea of the accused in the revision also more than 5 years had elapsed then to convert the trial into a warrant trial is totally uncalled for and deprived the petitioner of a single opportunity of hearing which was very much essential under the circumstances. Counsel prayed for setting aside the order dated 17.12.2015 passed in the Cr.R. No.83/2015 and prayed for a direction to the trial Court to convert the trial into a summary trial or in the alternative at least one opportunity of hearing be given in accordance with the Section 16-A of the Act to the trial Court. Counsel prayed that the orders passed by the Sessions Judge, Dewas on 21.12.2015 be [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order or transfer the case from the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dewas to another appropriate Court. Counsel submitted that the petitioner had lost its valuable right to cross-examine the witnesses and he placed reliance on Sunil Mehta and another Vs. State of Gujarat and another [(2013) 9 SCC 209], Balram Verma Vs. Union of India and others [1999 (1) JLJ 209] and Rekha Desai and anr. Vs. Rasiklal and ors. [1999(1) M.P.L.J.] and further Counsel submitted that the right of cross-examination was the right of every accused and to do substantial justice it was essential under the circumstances and prayed for setting aside the impugned order. has vehemently urged the fact that the orders passed by the trial Court as well as the revisional Court were in accordance with the provisions of law and more than 5 years had elapsed and the accused had himself admitted that he had no objection to the trial being converted into a warrant trial. Besides the trial Court had ample powers under Section 16-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act to convert the case from summary Jagjeet Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104226808/ 2 trial into a warrant trial and Counsel submitted that no adverse effect would be caused to the petitioner primarily because he would have chance to represent his case again at the time of framing of charge. She prayed that both the petitions are without merit and the same be dismissed. Considering the proviso which states thus:- "Section 16 A. Power of Court to try cases summarily 1[Power of Court to try cases summarily. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), all offences under subsection (1) of Sec. 16 shall be tried in a summary way by a Judicial Magistrate of the first class specially empowered in this behalf by the State Government or by a Metropolitan Magistrate and the provisions of Secs. 262 to 265 (both inclusive) of the said Code shall, as far is may be, apply to such trial: Provided that in the ease of any conviction in a summary trial under this section, it shall be lawful for the Magistrate to pass a sentence of imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year: Provided further that when at the commencement of, or in the course of a summary trial under this section, it appears to the Magistrate that the nature of the case is such that a sentence Of imprisonment for a term exceeding one year may have to be passed or that it is, for any other reason, undesirable to try the case summarily, the Magistrate shall after hearing the parties, record an order to that effect and thereafter recall any witness who may have been examined and proceed to hear or rehear the case in the manner provided by the said Code.]" 06. Counsel urged that hence the petitioner had moved the application for transfer of the case since valuable right had been lost to the petitioner to cross-examine which was rejected by the Sessions Judge and hence the present petition. Placing reliance in the matter of Harinarayan G. Bajaj Vs. State of Maharashtra [(2010) 11 SCC 520] the Apex Court held that:- Jagjeet Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104226808/ 3 "this Court reiterated the legal position stated in Ajoy Kumar Ghose and held that the right of an accused to cross-examine witnesses produced by the prosecution before framing of a charge against him was a valuable right.
